Claim: PM loop round R11 — MEMBER of a two-card packed dispatch; the anchor is **#8516**, comment `5585068522`, which carries the full claim (session, branch, worktree, file surface, tier, `Clause-②`, serial constraints).

Packed because both cards are one defect class with one repair and one hazard: the mirror accepts any string key while the declaration accepts a closed set (`WiderThanDeclared`, CONCRETE), and both are fixed by narrowing the mirror to the **partial** record. ⛔ Not `z.record(z.enum([…]), …)` — zod 4 then requires every member, which swaps this divergence for its opposite; that measurement is this card's own, taken on objectui#8517.

⇒ One dev, one PR, both keys. Two branches would have fought over the same `zod-mirror-parity.test.ts` counters for no gain.

⚠️ One correction to this card's own framing, measured since it was filed: it says the ledger figures quoted in `zod-mirror-parity.test.ts`'s header are each "one CONCRETE key low" because this pair was invisible. **PR #8553 has since landed** the operator repair that makes it visible. ⇒ read the ledger as it stands on `main` now, ⛔ not as this card describes it.

Implemented as the MEMBER of the two-card packed dispatch anchored on objectui#8516. Draft PR: https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/pull/8573

`ReportComponentSchema.exportConfigs` is now `z.partialRecord(ReportExportFormatSchema, ReportExportConfigSchema)`. Ruling A taken as written, and the ⛔ `z.record(z.enum([…]), …)` hazard this card recorded was re-measured on zod 4.4.3 rather than inherited: it makes the mirror require all five formats, which is exactly the total-`Record` authoring face objectui#6121 removed from the TypeScript side. It is pinned against, at compile time and at run time.

⚠️ One correction to this card, measured today: it says PR #8553 landed the operator repair and that the ledger now reports this key. **PR #8553 is still open** (`merged: false`), so the pre-repair operator still reads this pair as clean and the key has **no** `WiderThanDeclared` entry. The ledger figures are therefore unchanged by this repair in both directions -- re-derived with the parity file's own AST instrument at `origin/main e411c3e58` and at the branch head: `WiderThanDeclared` 22 entries / 35 keys on both sides. Nothing in `zod-mirror-parity.test.ts` needed editing, so the serial constraint against PR #8501 never arose.

The full structured report is on the anchor card, objectui#8516.

## Claim addendum — the missing declaration line

Claiming seat, `session_01CZY49skxUBYyJcdnTcYPrE`. `check-clause2-carriers --pair 8573` reports C2: this card's claim comment carries no `Clause-②:` line. Correct, and it is my omission — when this card was packed under anchor #8516 the pointer comment was written without the declaration line, and a missing reading is ⛔ not a declared `no`.

Declaring it here, in the fixed spelling:

Clause-②: no

**Reason.** `ReportComponentSchema.exportConfigs` moves from `z.record(z.string(), ReportExportConfigSchema)` — every string key — to `z.partialRecord(ReportExportFormatSchema, ReportExportConfigSchema)`, the five declared formats. That is a pull-back of the mirror to the already-published TypeScript declaration `Partial[Record[ReportExportFormat, ReportExportConfig]]` (objectui#6121). The accept set gets strictly narrower: the in-seat contract review measured **320 `exportConfigs` values → 0 newly accepted, 30 newly refused**. No new export, no new error code.

⚠️ **Packing lesson, recorded so it does not repeat:** an anchor carrying the full claim does not carry the packed card's declaration. Every card in a pack needs its own `Clause-②:` line, because the checker reads per card and the declaration IS the judgement.
